title: The Smith chart
blurb: Read a Smith chart: resistance circles, reactance arcs, the matched center, SWR circles and wavelength scales, and use it to place a stub.

E9G01.why: The chart tracks how impedance changes **along a transmission line**. It says nothing about radiation, patterns or propagation.

E9G02.why: A point is fixed by where a **resistance circle** meets a **reactance arc**.
E9G02.trap: Voltage and current aren't plotted. The chart is a map of impedance.

E9G03.why: Smith charts give **impedance and SWR** along a line. Headings, bearings and propagation use other tools.

E9G04.why: The two families are **constant-resistance circles** and **constant-reactance arcs**.
E9G04.trap: Inductive and capacitive are just the sign of the reactance, not families.

E9G05.why: Its classic job: the **position and length of a matching stub**. Slide to the g = 1 circle, then cancel what is left.

E9G06.why: Every reactance arc ends on the **outer circle** (r = 0), which is the **reactance axis**.

E9G07.why: Everything else curves. The straight horizontal line (x = 0) is the **resistance axis**.

E9G08.why: Impedances are divided by Z₀, so you **reassign the center's value** to the line's impedance: 1 + j0.

E9G09.why: Moving along a line keeps SWR constant, so the point circles the center: a **constant-SWR circle**.

E9G10.why: The arcs are points of **constant reactance**. The circles are constant resistance.

E9G11.why: The rim scales count **fractions of a wavelength along the line**. Half a wavelength is one lap.
E9G11.trap: Frequency isn't on the scale, and it is the line's wavelength, not the antenna's.
